explanation: The G190A substitution introduces a methyl side chain into the NNRTI pocket core that creates a steric clash with efavirenz, despite being only 3.7 Å from the ligand—close enough for van der Waals contact repulsion. Glycine's conformational flexibility at this position permits efavirenz accommodation, whereas alanine's rigid methyl group occupies space that the inhibitor requires, forcing unfavorable repositioning or partial unbinding. This ~29 Ų volume expansion at a direct contact point destabilizes the ligand-binding geometry without altering electrostatics, explaining the 0.70 kcal/mol binding penalty.
